chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Jamil and Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Jamil, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم cursed whoever introduces an offense in al-Madinah or gives shelter to an offender.” I said: “What is that offense?” He said: “Killing.”

key_terms.الْقَتْلُ: killing; the offense explicitly identified by the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: al-Madinah, the sacred city referred to in the report
key_terms.حَدَثًا: a grave offense or violation introduced within the city
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.لَعَنَ: invoked curse upon; condemned in the strongest terms
key_terms.مُحْدِثًا: one who commits such an offense

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about committing or sheltering murder in al-Madinah?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم condemned introducing grave violation in al-Madinah or sheltering the one who commits it. The Imam عليه السلام explains that the intended offense here is killing, indicating the severe sanctity of the sacred precinct and the gravity of murder within it.
